findings: Surface generation is primarily deterministic skeleton/template assembly, not open-ended language generation.
Variation pools change wording but preserve a finite phrase inventory.
AnswerContentIR provides dynamic facts/conditions/reasons, so content is not wholly canned.
Dialogue interpretation is regex and rule oriented; semantic frames add structure but do not create unrestricted linguistic competence.
Runtime candidate selection chooses among generated skeleton candidates; it does not synthesize arbitrary wording beyond registered components.
Caching and stable signatures may repeat identical wording for identical IR/persona inputs.
Surface diversity checks reduce recent repetition but do not remove template dependence.
